questions.problem:

questions.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) & =(-3)(x-2)(x-(-5)) \\  & =-3(x-2)(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-3(x-2)(x+5) & =-3({x}^{2}+5x-2x-10) \\  & =-3({x}^{2}+3x-10) \\  & =-3{x}^{2}-9x+30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-3{x}^{2}-9x+30.$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(1)(z-2\text{i})(z-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i}) & ={z}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)={z}^{2}+4.$

questions.problem: Which of the following is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(v)=-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$

Next, we solve $f(v)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(v) & =0 \\ -{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =0 \\ {v}^{2}-12v+45 & =0 \\ ({v}^{2}-2\cdot 6\cdot v+{6}^{2})-{6}^{2}+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}-36+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =-9 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (v-6)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ v-6 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ v & =6\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${v}_{1}=6+3\text{i}$ and ${v}_{2}=6-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-1,$ the expression $-{v}^{2}+12v-45$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}-{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =a(v-{v}_{1})(v-{v}_{2}) \\  & =-(v-(6+3\text{i}))(v-(6-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $v-(6-3\text{i})$ is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$

Next, we solve $f(u)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+5 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2\cdot u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+5 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-4 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(2\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${u}_{1}=1+2\text{i}$ and ${u}_{2}=1-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression ${u}^{2}-2u+5$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+5 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+2\text{i}))(u-(1-2\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $u-(1-2\text{i})$ is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5.$

Next, we solve $f(u) = 0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+10 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}-1+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-9 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots $u_1=1+ 3\textrm{i}$ and $u_2=1- 3\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression $u^2-2u+10$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+10 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+3\text{i}))(u-(1-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$
